newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent sheds 20 cents, other North Sea steady.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent sheds 20 cents, other North Sea steady.

text.p: Dated Brent crude dropped about 20 cents on Tuesday and was set for further losses after a spell of shortcovering petered out, but other North Sea grades were holding their ground, traders said.
An Aug 18-20 cargo traded at Sept Brent +18 cents, the equivalent of 10 cents below an August-related deal on Friday, before one of Tuesday's dates fetched Sept Brent +3 cents in late trade.
"Most of the market realised that the Brent deals we saw last week were a bit high. Dated was certainly overinflated," said a potential seller.
All three Aug 20-22 Brents turning wet on Tuesday were kept ahead of the five o'clock deadline, two to BP and the third, a deferred Aug 19-21 loader to Aron.

Traders said the market was quiet with buyers still holding back for further news from Iraq. Baghdad was expected to submit its pricing formula for a second round of oil exports later on Tuesday, according to a well-placed Arab envoy in New York.

IPE Sept Brent shrugged off the news -- losing just five cents to $19.41 a barrel by 1723 GMT -- but cash markets weakened, Aug/Sep trading at +25 cents, down from +30 on Monday, and Sep/Oct talked at -5/-3 cents after earlier trade at evens.
Other North Sea crudes failed to react to Dated's slide, Ekofisk holding Monday's traded level of Dated Brent +30 cents and Oseberg even edging a couple of cents higher to +29.5 cents.
Statfjord was struggling, however, with at least a handful of August cargoes still to be placed.

Mediterranean sour markets were teetering on the edge of a precipice as traders waited for a clear indication of how soon Iraqi exports would be flowing again from the Turkish port of Ceyhan and at what rate.
"(Russian) Urals could lose $1 once Iraqi oil starts flowing again," said a trader.
Nigerian crude eased as late August loading cargoes struggled to find homes across the Atlantic.
With Asian demand covered, about 10 million barrels of sweet crude were still available this month, most offered on a delivered basis to cautious buyers in the U.S. Gulf.
"The U.S. is very slow at the moment," said a trader.
Dealing was also subdued as equity holders awaited the release of the September loading schedules due this week.
Bonny Light was pegged a couple of cents lower at around Dated Brent +45 cents. Forcados was also seen softer at about Dated Brent +30 cents.
August loadings of Oso condensate were delayed by up to 14 days after field operator Mobil shut down production early last week following a technical failure.

Traders said a Mobil cargo due to load last weekend had been delayed to August 16th and two cargoes belonging to NNPC, Mobil's Oso joint venture partner, and a further Mobil cargo were subject to similar delays.
Mobil said it planned to restart Oso production on Tuesday, reaching the normal 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) level "in a few days".
